citations.quote: a set $F$ is closed exactly when
Every ordinal $\alpha \in \omega_1$ is at most countable
any two disjoint closed sets can be separated by
any two distinct points are separated by disjoint open sets
Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function

derivations.claim: Singletons are closed, inactive points isolated, initial segments open and inactive-cut initial segments clopen; W_n is open.
inputs: active indices are limits; lower-level ladders

derivations.claim: A disjoint closed pair has a countable bounded member.
inputs: common cofinal ladder intersection forces membership in both closed sets

derivations.claim: Enumerating a countable family and removing finitely many bounded intersections yields disjoint cofinal tails and the full omega-color almost-P0 property.
inputs: finite list or omega enumeration; least bounds; default color zero

derivations.claim: A clopen countable successor cut contains K_0; one fixed disjoint-tail family provides a deterministic extension operation for all later colorings.
The two color conditions and exclusion of the opposite old set produce disjoint monotone expansions, with H_0' below xi.
inputs: disjoint closed H_0,H_1 with H_0 subset xi

derivations.claim: A cofinal ladder intersection outside an expanded set is impossible, proving its closedness.
inputs: old intersection bounded; new points below xi; inactive xi; eventually-zero extension at alpha outside H_i

derivations.claim: Every old active point below xi has a ladder tail inside its expansion.
inputs: eventual colors (1,0); opposite closed set has bounded intersection

derivations.claim: Finite iteration yields nested disjoint closed pairs with tail inclusion; their unions define U_0,U_1.
inputs: fixed extension operation; no sequence of unspecified choices

derivations.claim: The unions are disjoint open neighborhoods of the original pair, giving normality and Hausdorff separation of closed singletons.
inputs: maximum of two finite stage indices

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 uses an empty enumeration and zero extension; step 2.1 chooses xi=1 if K_0 is empty; step 6.1 covers empty closed members.
Step 1.3 uses epsilon_0=0 and default color zero; step 5.1 starts from stage zero.
Step 1.1 proves singleton closedness; step 1.3 covers a one-ladder enumeration; step 6.1 separates singleton pairs.
Step 1.3 permits repeated color values and finite or empty active families; the disjoint tails make assignment unambiguous.
Step 1.1 treats alpha=xi separately by inactivity; step 4.1 excludes equality at the successor cut.

AC supplies the countable boundedness fact in step 1.2; step 1.3 fixes one countable enumeration. Step 2.1 fixes all tails once; step 5.1 iterates an explicit operation without further witness choices.

boundaries.reason: This is a sufficiency theorem under a supplied AD system; the closedness equivalence is already proved by its declared topology supplier.
No converse from normal Hausdorff spaces to AD systems or almost-P0 is asserted.
